Please help us improve our site! × No thank you American Civil Liberties UnionThe American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is an organization founded in 1920, with the mission of defending and preserving the individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the U.S. Constitution. The ACLU currently has more than 1.7 million members, 500 staff attorneys, thousands of volunteer attorneys, and several offices throughout the United States. Within its organizational mission, the ACLU engages in activities such as litigation, legislative lobbying, and educational outreach to:Fight for racial justice.Maintain freedom of and from religion.Preserve freedom of speech.Defend liberty in times of national crisis.Apply the Bill of Rights within the criminal justice system.Protect women’s equality.Safeguard reproductive freedom.Fight for equality for the LGBTQ+ community.Guarantee the right to vote.For detailed information about the ACLU, visit their website: www.aclu.org [Last reviewed in June of 2022 by the Wex Definitions Team]Keywordslawsuits-courtWexACADEMIC TOPICS trial process/advocacy CIVICS civil rights human rights the Constitution THE LEGAL PROCESS class actions courts wex definitions civil procedure constitutional law government Wex Toolbox Sponsored ListingsRebecca Lynne Melone PREMIUM(888) 345-7848Reston, VA Family Law, Divorce, Estate PlanningWebsiteEmailCallEmailProfileMatthew Crowley PREMIUM(571) 609-5681Fairfax, VA Criminal Law, DUI & DWI, Juvenile Law, Traffic Tickets, Domestic ViolenceWebsiteEmailCallEmailProfileWilfred Yeargan PREMIUM(703) 352-9044Fairfax, VA Criminal Law, DUI & DWI, Traffic Tickets, Personal Injury, Business LawWebsiteEmailCallEmailProfileFaisal Moghul PREMIUM(703) 652-5506Leesburg, VA Business Law, Construction Law, Landlord Tenant, Real Estate LawWebsiteEmailCallEmailProfileTerry Lee Fox PREMIUM(703) 652-5506Leesburg, VA Real Estate Law, Business Law, Construction Law, TrademarksWebsiteEmailCallEmailProfileFaraji A.
